1 /* 2 * Copyright 2002-2017 the original author or authors. 3 * 4 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"); 5 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. 6 * You may obtain a copy of the License at 7 * 8 * http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 9 * 10 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software 11 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, 12 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied. 13 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and 14 * limitations under the License. 15 */ 16 package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.service; 17 18 import java.util.Locale; 19 20 import org.springframework.stereotype.Component; 21 22 /** 23 * Derives a household's stable, shared identifier from its last name and postcode. 24 * 25 *

Owners belong to the same household when they share a last name (compared 26 * case-insensitively and ignoring differences in surrounding or repeated whitespace) 27 * and postcode. Because the identifier is a deterministic hash of that normalized 28 * identity, every owner in a household maps to the same value automatically, 29 * independently and across requests, without any owner having to opt in. 30 */ 31 @Component 32 public class HouseholdIdGenerator { 33 34 private static final int ID_LENGTH = 12; 35 36 /** 37 * Build the shared household identifier for the household identified by the given 38 * last name and postcode: the first {@value #ID_LENGTH} hex characters of the 39 * SHA-256 digest of {@code normalizedLastName + '|' + postcode}. 40 * 41 *

An owner without a postcode belongs to no shared household, so this returns 42 * {@code null} in that case. 43 * 44 * @param lastName the household's last name 45 * @param postcode the household's postcode 46 * @return the stable household identifier, e.g. {@code "0a1b2c3d4e5f"}, or 47 * {@code null} when no postcode is supplied 48 */ 49 public String generate(String lastName, String postcode) { 50 if (postcode == null || postcode.isBlank()) { 51 return null; 52 } 53 String identity = normalize(lastName) + "|" + postcode; 54 return Sha256.hex(identity).substring(0, ID_LENGTH); 55 } 56 57 /** 58 * Normalize the last name for comparison: trim, collapse each run of whitespace to 59 * a single space and lower-case, so that differences in case or spacing do not 60 * split what is really one household. 61 */ 62 private static String normalize(String value) { 63 if (value == null) { 64 return ""; 65 } 66 return value.strip().replaceAll("\\s+", " ").toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT); 67 } 68 } 69

`AcceptanceTest` is the only test class, and it passes. The change is complete.

## Summary

I implemented customerCode de-duplication so that when a computed code collides with an existing owner's code, `-<n>` is appended with the smallest `n ≥ 2` that makes it unique.

The logic was placed where each piece belongs:

1. **`CustomerCodeGenerator.generateUnique(...)`** — The generator owns the customerCode *format*, so the suffix-appending logic lives here. It derives the base code via the existing `generate(...)` (reused, not copied) and appends `-2`, `-3`, … until a candidate isn't taken. Store access is kept out of this class by taking a `Predicate<String> isTaken`.

2. **`OwnerRepository.existsByCustomerCode(String)`** — A new query method, implemented in all three repository flavors following the existing `countBy...` patterns:
   - `SpringDataOwnerRepository` — Spring Data derived query.
   - `JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl` — JPQL count.
   - `JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl` — SQL count on `customer_code`.

3. **`ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner(...)`** — Now calls `generateUnique(..., ownerRepository::existsByCustomerCode)`, wiring the store-existence check into the generator. The service keeps its orchestration role without absorbing formatting logic.

## Summary

I implemented customerCode de-duplication so that when a computed code collides with an existing owner's code, `-<n>` is appended with the smallest `n ≥ 2` that makes it unique.

The logic was placed where each piece belongs:

1. **`CustomerCodeGenerator.generateUnique(...)`** — The generator owns the customerCode *format*, so the suffix-appending logic lives here. It derives the base code via the existing `generate(...)` (reused, not copied) and appends `-2`, `-3`, … until a candidate isn't taken. Store access is kept out of this class by taking a `Predicate<String> isTaken`.

2. **`OwnerRepository.existsByCustomerCode(String)`** — A new query method, implemented in all three repository flavors following the existing `countBy...` patterns:
   - `SpringDataOwnerRepository` — Spring Data derived query.
   - `JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl` — JPQL count.
   - `JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl` — SQL count on `customer_code`.

3. **`ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner(...)`** — Now calls `generateUnique(..., ownerRepository::existsByCustomerCode)`, wiring the store-existence check into the generator. The service keeps its orchestration role without absorbing formatting logic.

The de-duplicated `customerCode` is stored on the owner (and thus returned), and the test suite is green.
